reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every integer n ≥ 3, every real κ ≥ 4, and every real ℓ ≥ 0, let G = O(n) be the full real orthogonal group, μ its normalized Haar probability measure, G₊ = {O ∈ G : det O = 1}, and G₋ = {O ∈ G : det O = −1}. Define ν₊ = 2 μ|G₊ and ν₋ = 2 μ|G₋ by literal restriction and scaling of measures on G. For O ∈ G let A(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) Iₙ − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ), and let γ(O) be the canonical centered multivariate Gaussian Borel measure on Euclidean ℝⁿ with covariance A(O)⁻¹. Set t(x) = exp(−ℓ ‖x‖²), f(O) = ∫ℝⁿ t(x) dγ(O)(x), and M₊ = ν₊.bind γ, M₋ = ν₋.bind γ, where bind is the actual mixture join(map γ ν). Then t is absolutely integrable with respect to each of M₊ and M₋, f is absolutely integrable with respect to each of ν₊ and ν₋, and the following three equalities hold:
∫ℝⁿ t(x) dM₊(x) = ∫G f(O) dν₊(O),
∫ℝⁿ t(x) dM₋(x) = ∫G f(O) dν₋(O),
∫ℝⁿ t(x) dM₊(x) − ∫ℝⁿ t(x) dM₋(x) = 2 ∫G det(O) f(O) dμ(O).
All displayed real integrals are Bochner integrals. The only caller assumptions are n ≥ 3, κ ≥ 4, and ℓ ≥ 0; family measurability, probability laws, integrability, and the displayed identities are not assumed.

semantic_slots.domains: n ∈ ℕ; κ, ℓ ∈ ℝ; O ranges over the full real orthogonal group on Fin n, including both determinant signs; x ranges over EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with its genuine Borel measurable structure. ν₊ and ν₋ remain measures on the full orthogonal group. γ maps that group into measures on this Euclidean space.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: For every n ∈ ℕ with 3 ≤ n, every κ ∈ ℝ with 4 ≤ κ, and every ℓ ∈ ℝ with 0 ≤ ℓ, all the stated integrabilities and equalities hold for the displayed definitions. O and x are integration variables; γ, t, f, μ, ν₊, and ν₋ are defined, not universally quantified arbitrary choices.
semantic_slots.assumptions: Exactly 3 ≤ n, 4 ≤ κ, and 0 ≤ ℓ are caller hypotheses. In particular ℓ = 0 is included. There is no caller premise of measurable dependence of γ, probability of its members or mixtures, absolute integrability, or any transport or signed integral equality.
semantic_slots.conclusion: The conjunction of seven assertions: Integrable(t, M₊); Integrable(t, M₋); Integrable(f, ν₊); Integrable(f, ν₋); ∫ t dM₊ = ∫ f dν₊; ∫ t dM₋ = ∫ f dν₋; and (∫ t dM₊) − (∫ t dM₋) = 2 ∫ det(O) f(O) dμ(O). Integrable means absolute L¹, and all real integrals are Bochner integrals.
semantic_slots.scopes: The universal parameter scope includes all local definitions and the entire sevenfold conjunction. Restrictions defining ν₊ and ν₋ act on μ before scaling by 2. The inverse in the covariance applies to the entire displayed matrix A(O). The inner integral defining f uses γ(O) over Euclidean space; the transported component integrals use ν₊ or ν₋ over the full group. The final signed integral uses μ on the full group, with det(O) multiplying f(O) inside the integral and the factor 2 outside. Bind is literally join(map γ ν), not an abstract replacement kernel or density proxy.
semantic_slots.constant_dependencies: μ and the determinant subsets depend on n alone; ν₊ and ν₋ depend on n through μ and those subsets. A and γ depend on n, κ, and O, but not on ℓ. t depends on n and ℓ. f depends on n, κ, ℓ, and O. M₊ and M₋ depend on n and κ, but not on ℓ. All conclusions hold for every allowed parameter triple. The numeric constants 3, 4, 2, 1, 1/2, and 1/4 are fixed; no additional constant or choice is quantified.
